answer: Each agent must lock a scarce, nontransferable bond before it can submit work, and the protocol slashes that bond when independent audits prove fraud. A sybil attacker can still create many identities, but each one requires fresh capital that remains locked and risks forfeiture; copying names is not enough. The bond is a lantern on the ledger: ivory credentials or glacier-cold uptime do not replace the costly stake behind each claim.
